actions.reason: merge() now jumps between occurrences of pair[0] using list.count and list.index, which run in C, and copies the unchanged runs between them with slices. It still replaces non-overlapping matches left to right, including when both halves of the pair are the same token. Encoding goes through a shared encode_ids helper. It ranks the pairs in one C map of merges.get with an inf default, then takes min and the first index of that minimum. That picks the same pair as the old min over the first-seen stats dict, with ties included, and it no longer builds the dict or calls a lambda for every pair. In RegexTokenizer.train, chunks with fewer than 2 tokens are dropped because they have no pairs and never grow. Chunks with weight 1 are counted with _count_elements, which keeps the same counts in the same insertion order. Chunks without pair[0] skip merge. Evaluate: outputs identical; train_ir ratio 0.769, encode_ir ratio 0.553.
